We also gradually eliminate the logical gaps in our stories—characteristic of our earlier stage of perception—as intense preoccupation with the whole vision gives way to preoccupation with correctness. At this stage our vocabulary is firmly grounded. We use words everyone else uses. We have little need to invent metaphors to communicate.
